title.narrative: International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange (IODE) – global ocean data and information systems

description.narrative:
Since 1961 this programme has built a worldwide network of national centres that manage and share ocean data, information and expertise. It operates global online systems — including the Ocean Data and Information System (ODIS), which connects ocean datasets and products across countries and partners, the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), a catalogue of scientific publications and a directory of ocean experts — making ocean knowledge freely findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable for governments, researchers and the public. The programme also works with the Commission's capacity development activities to build national expertise. These data, tools and standards inform decisions on climate change, ocean health, ocean hazards and a sustainable ocean economy, and underpin global reporting on the Sustainable Development Goals and other international ocean agreements.
The following key topics are the key areas of the 2026-2027 workplan: 1. Overarching issues including IODE governance, IOC Member State engagement, Communications, the ocean expert website 2. IOC Data Architecture, national oceanographic data centres (NODC)/ Associate Data Units (ADU) engagement and ODIS 3. OBIS 4. Programme Activities, particularly World Ocean Database 5. Intersessional Working Group on data in national jurisdiction 6. Capacity Development for SIDS - and quality management for NODCs
